correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the inverse at fixed output X. Positive predator output requires x=t+u with u>0. Set delta=epsilon-X. For delta>0 the allowable source interval is 0<u<u0, where r(qu0+u0^2)=delta, and Y=(b/a)u(delta-rqu-ru^2)/(t+u). It is positive in this interval, zero at both endpoints, and its derivative has the sign of delta-rR_t(u), strictly decreasing through zero. This proves the full two/one/none census and gives the stated Y_f at the only stationary point; delta<=0 has no positive predecessor, including the threshold. Multiplying (q+2u)u^2 by R_t'(u) gives the derivative of P_t, so integration in X gives the exact area. Uniformly in U, u_X=epsilon(1-U)/(2rq)+O(epsilon^2), giving V_f=(1-U)^2/4+O(epsilon) and the cubic area with coefficient b/(12atrq). The scaled inverse equations are V=xi*eta and U=1-xi-eta+O(epsilon), with a smooth exact remainder. The two limiting solutions are positive, and the Jacobian in (xi,eta) is nonsingular when xi differs from eta, giving both interior branch limits. These arguments validate the continuum statements independently of the finite supplied checker, which was inspected, not run. The restriction t>1 is sufficient and makes the critical immigration positive; the wording that strict t>1 is essential should not be read as a claim of failure at t=1, where the same calculation has critical immigration zero.
